newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up vs spot dlr, fwd premiums drop.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up vs spot dlr, fwd premiums drop.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Tuesday at 35.83/84 per dollar, up from Monday's close of 35.84/85 after dropping to an intraday low of 35.855, dealers said.
They said the rupee traded at a high of 35.835 and a low of 35.855 on Tuesday.
Dealers said Tuesday's trade was largely driven by dollar purchases by the State Bank of India (SBI).
"The rupee opened at 35.835/845 and was stuck in a 35.835/840 band for much of the morning," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"Then SBI bought dollars late morning and the rupee dropped to 35.855 at one stage," he said. "But the rupee rallied when SBI went off the market in the afternoon."
Dealers said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) did not buy dollars on Tuesday. RBI bought dollars in small amounts on Monday.
The central bank's dollar purchases pushed the rupee down from its opening of 35.75 last Monday.
Dealers said the rupee ended up against the dollar in the forward market on dollar sales by corporates.
They said forward premiums opened down on easier domestic liquidity and expectations of falling call money rates.
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Tuesday at 4.41 percent against Monday's close of 4.52 percent.
